summaryBox.takeaway: Cardiac cycle lasts 0.8s. LUB = AV valve closure at start of ventricular systole; DUP = Semilunar valve closure at diastole. Stroke Volume = EDV - ESV = 120 - 50 = 70 mL. Cardiac Output = SV × HR ≈ 5.0 L/min.

conceptBreakdown.content:
The **Cardiac Cycle** represents the sequential events of atrial and ventricular contraction (**Systole**) and relaxation (**Diastole**) during a single heartbeat. At a resting heart rate of $75\text{ beats/min}$, one cardiac cycle lasts **$0.8\text{ seconds}$**.

### 6.1 Mechanical Phases of the Cardiac Cycle
1. **Joint Diastole ($0.4\text{ s}$)**: All 4 chambers relaxed; AV valves open; Semilunar valves closed; $70\%$ passive ventricular filling.
2. **Atrial Systole ($0.1\text{ s}$)**: Atria contract; pumps remaining $30\%$ blood into ventricles (Atrial Kick), reaching $\text{EDV} \approx 120\text{ mL}$.
3. **Ventricular Systole ($0.3\text{ s}$)**: Isovolumetric contraction closes AV valves (**"LUB"**); Semilunar valves open, ejecting Stroke Volume ($\text{SV} \approx 70\text{ mL}$).
4. **Ventricular Diastole ($0.5\text{ s}$)**: Ventricles relax; Semilunar valves close (**"DUP"**).

### 6.2 Volumetric Bioenergetics & Cardiac Output
$$\text{Stroke Volume (SV)} = \text{EDV} - \text{ESV} = 120\text{ mL} - 50\text{ mL} = \mathbf{70\text{ mL}}$$
$$\text{Cardiac Output (CO)} = \text{SV} \times \text{HR} = 70\text{ mL} \times 72\text{ bpm} \approx \mathbf{5040\text{ mL/min} (5.0\text{ L/min})}$$
- **Frank-Starling Law**: Within physiological limits, force of contraction is directly proportional to initial muscle fiber stretch (End-Diastolic Volume).
